      "snippet": "Short answer: yes.
If we actually follow this 3-layer, microkernel-style design, a ton of what’s currently crammed into persistent memory gets moved into:

CI (NS kernel) = invariants, meta-rules, boot behavior

Files (/mnt/data) = full OS modules

Memory = only dynamic kernel-state

That does free memory headroom for new learning and reduces drift.
Now I’ll do the useful thing: turn Grok’s giant research dump into a real NS-style CI kernel you can paste into Custom Instructions.
